units.title: Unit 1: Conservation of Matter & Periodic Properties

lessons.title: Part 1: Elements, Compounds, Mixtures & Conservation of Matter
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Conservation of Atoms in Chemical Reactions
lessons.reading: An element is made of one kind of atom, while a compound has two or more elements chemically bonded together. A mixture blends substances physically without chemical bonds. During any chemical reaction, atoms rearrange into new molecules, so total mass is always conserved.

principles.title: Elements, Compounds, Mixtures & Conservation of Matter
principles.summary: Atoms rearrange during chemical reactions, so total mass stays the same.

bank.prompt: What is a pure substance made of one atom type?
bank.explanation: An element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atom, like gold or oxygen.

bank.prompt: What forms when two elements chemically bond together?
bank.explanation: A compound is a substance formed when two or more elements chemically bond in a fixed ratio.

bank.prompt: How are substances combined inside a mixture?
bank.explanation: A mixture combines substances physically so each substance keeps its own chemical identity.

bank.prompt: What happens to total mass during a chemical reaction?
bank.explanation: Conservation of matter means matter is neither created nor destroyed during a chemical reaction.

bank.prompt: What happens to atoms during a chemical change?
bank.explanation: In a chemical reaction, existing atoms break apart and rearrange to form new products.

bank.prompt: What is a uniform mixture like salt water called?
bank.explanation: A solution is a homogeneous mixture where one substance dissolves evenly into another.

bank.prompt: If 10 grams of reactants react in a sealed jar, what is the product mass?
bank.explanation: By conservation of mass, the mass of products equals the starting mass of reactants.

bank.prompt: Which example shows a chemical compound?
choices: Water made of hydrogen and oxygen
Trail mix with nuts and raisins
bank.answer: Water made of hydrogen and oxygen
bank.explanation: Water (H2O) is a compound because hydrogen and oxygen atoms are chemically bonded together.

lessons.title: Part 2: Periodic Table Groups & Physical vs. Chemical Properties
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Periodic Table Groups & Properties of Matter
lessons.reading: Vertical columns on the periodic table are called groups or families. Elements in the same group have similar outer electrons and react in similar ways. Physical properties like melting point and conductivity can be observed without changing the substance, while chemical properties like rusting or pH describe how it reacts.

principles.title: Periodic Table Groups & Physical vs. Chemical Properties
principles.summary: Elements in the same column share similar chemical properties.

bank.prompt: What are columns on the periodic table called?
bank.explanation: Groups are vertical columns on the periodic table whose elements have similar chemical behavior.

bank.prompt: Why do elements in the same group react similarly?
choices: They were discovered the same year
bank.explanation: Chemical reactivity depends on outer electrons, which match within a periodic table group.

bank.prompt: Which trait is a physical property of matter?
bank.explanation: A physical property can be measured without changing the substance into something new.

bank.prompt: Which trait is a chemical property of matter?
bank.explanation: A chemical property describes how a substance reacts to form a new substance.

bank.prompt: Where are metals located on the periodic table?
choices: Only in the far right column
bank.explanation: Metals occupy the left and middle sections of the periodic table and conduct heat well.

bank.prompt: What property makes copper useful for electrical wires?
bank.explanation: Electrical conductivity is a physical property allowing electric current to flow easily through metals.

bank.prompt: Why are noble gases in Group 18 mostly unreactive?
choices: Their outer electron shells are full
bank.answer: Their outer electron shells are full
bank.explanation: Noble gases have full outer electron shells, so they rarely form chemical bonds.

bank.prompt: What does acidity or pH measure in a liquid?
choices: How acidic or basic it is
bank.answer: How acidic or basic it is
bank.explanation: The pH scale measures whether a solution is an acid, neutral, or a base.

units.title: Unit 2: Earth’s Water, Atmosphere, Moon Cycles & Ecosystems

lessons.title: Part 1: Hydrologic Cycle, Ocean Currents & Atmosphere
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: The Water Cycle, Ocean Currents & Atmosphere
lessons.reading: Sunlight powers evaporation and transpiration, while gravity pulls precipitation down as rain or snow. In the oceans, cold salty water is denser and sinks to drive deep currents, while warm surface currents warm nearby coasts. Most weather happens in the troposphere, Earth’s lowest atmospheric layer.

principles.title: Hydrologic Cycle, Ocean Currents & Earth Atmosphere
principles.summary: Solar energy and gravity drive water movement, winds, and ocean currents.

bank.prompt: What main energy source powers the water cycle?
bank.explanation: Solar energy warms liquid water on Earth, causing evaporation into the atmosphere.

bank.prompt: What force pulls rain and snow back to Earth?
bank.explanation: Gravity pulls condensed water droplets down as precipitation and moves runoff downhill.

bank.prompt: What happens during condensation in the sky?
choices: Water vapor cools into liquid drops
bank.answer: Water vapor cools into liquid drops
bank.explanation: Condensation occurs when rising water vapor cools and changes into liquid cloud droplets.

bank.prompt: What causes deep ocean density currents to sink?
bank.explanation: Cold, salty ocean water is denser than warm water, so it sinks and drives deep currents.

bank.prompt: In which atmospheric layer does most weather occur?
bank.explanation: The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere and holds most water vapor and weather.

bank.prompt: What is the release of water vapor from plant leaves?
bank.explanation: Transpiration is the process where plants release water vapor into the air through tiny leaf pores.

bank.prompt: How do warm surface ocean currents affect nearby coasts?
bank.explanation: Warm ocean currents transfer thermal energy to the air, creating milder coastal temperatures.

bank.prompt: Which gas is most abundant in Earth’s atmosphere?
bank.explanation: Earth’s atmosphere is about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen.

lessons.title: Part 2: Earth-Moon-Sun Cycles: Tides, Eclipses & Phases
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Moon Phases, Eclipses, Seasons & Ocean Tides
lessons.reading: The Moon’s gravity pulls on Earth’s oceans to create daily high and low tides. When the Sun, Earth, and Moon align during new and full moons, extra-strong spring tides occur. A solar eclipse happens when the Moon blocks sunlight, while a lunar eclipse happens when Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon.

principles.title: Earth-Moon-Sun Cycles: Tides, Eclipses & Phases
principles.summary: Positions of Earth, Moon, and Sun cause moon phases, eclipses, and ocean tides.

bank.prompt: What is the main cause of daily ocean tides?
bank.explanation: Tides are regular rises and falls of ocean water caused mainly by the Moon’s gravity.

bank.prompt: When do extra-high spring tides happen?
bank.explanation: Spring tides occur when the Sun, Earth, and Moon line up, combining their gravitational pull.

bank.prompt: What happens during a solar eclipse?
choices: The Moon blocks sunlight from Earth
Earth blocks light to the Moon
bank.answer: The Moon blocks sunlight from Earth
bank.explanation: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes directly between the Sun and Earth.

bank.prompt: What causes the different phases of the Moon?
choices: Viewing the lit Moon from angles
Earth’s shadow covering the Moon daily
The Moon spinning on a tilt
bank.answer: Viewing the lit Moon from angles
bank.explanation: Moon phases change as the Moon orbits Earth and we see different portions of its sunlit side.

bank.prompt: What causes a lunar eclipse?
choices: Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon
The Moon moves in front of Venus
bank.answer: Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon
bank.explanation: A lunar eclipse happens when Earth is directly between the Sun and a full Moon.

bank.prompt: When do moderate neap tides occur?
choices: During first and third quarter moons
When Earth is closest to Mars
bank.answer: During first and third quarter moons
bank.explanation: Neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon pull at right angles, making smaller tidal ranges.

bank.prompt: Why does Earth experience four seasons each year?
choices: Earth’s tilted axis as it orbits
Earth moving closer to the Moon
bank.answer: Earth’s tilted axis as it orbits
bank.explanation: Seasons happen because Earth’s axis is tilted 23.5 degrees as it revolves around the Sun.

bank.prompt: About how long does one full cycle of Moon phases take?
bank.explanation: A lunar cycle from one new moon to the next takes about 29.5 days.

lessons.title: Part 3: Matter & Energy Flow in Ecosystems & Biomes
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Photosynthesis, Energy Pyramids & Biomes
lessons.reading: Producers use photosynthesis to turn sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen. Consumers and decomposers use cellular respiration to release that energy and recycle nutrients. Because most energy escapes as heat at each level, higher trophic levels have less available energy.

principles.title: Matter & Energy Flow in Ecosystems & Biomes
principles.summary: Producers capture solar energy while matter cycles among organisms and the environment.

bank.prompt: What process do plants use to make food from sunlight?
bank.explanation: Photosynthesis uses sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make glucose sugar and oxygen.

bank.prompt: What is the role of decomposers in an ecosystem?
choices: Break down dead matter for nutrients
bank.answer: Break down dead matter for nutrients
bank.explanation: Decomposers like fungi and bacteria recycle nutrients from dead organisms back into the soil.

bank.prompt: What gas do plants release during photosynthesis?
bank.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen gas as a product of photosynthesis.

bank.prompt: How do cells release energy from sugar during respiration?
bank.explanation: Cellular respiration uses oxygen to break down glucose, releasing energy, water, and carbon dioxide.

bank.prompt: What happens to available energy moving up an energy pyramid?
choices: Most energy is lost as heat
bank.answer: Most energy is lost as heat
bank.explanation: Only about 10 percent of energy passes to the next level; the rest escapes as heat.

bank.prompt: Which two factors mainly define a land biome?
bank.explanation: A biome is a large region characterized by its average temperature, rainfall, and plant life.

bank.prompt: Which biome has permanently frozen soil called permafrost?
bank.explanation: The tundra is a cold, treeless biome with a frozen soil layer called permafrost.

bank.prompt: What are organisms that make their own food called?
bank.explanation: Producers make their own food using energy from sunlight and form the base of food webs.

bank.explanation: Transpiration is the process where plants release water vapor into the air through tiny leaf pores.

bank.prompt: How do warm surface ocean currents affect nearby coasts?
bank.explanation: Warm ocean currents transfer thermal energy to the air, creating milder coastal temperatures.

bank.prompt: Which gas is most abundant in Earth’s atmosphere?
bank.explanation: Earth’s atmosphere is about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen.

principles.title: Earth-Moon-Sun Cycles: Tides, Eclipses & Phases
principles.summary: Positions of Earth, Moon, and Sun cause moon phases, eclipses, and ocean tides.

bank.prompt: What is the main cause of daily ocean tides?
bank.explanation: Tides are regular rises and falls of ocean water caused mainly by the Moon’s gravity.

bank.prompt: When do extra-high spring tides happen?
bank.explanation: Spring tides occur when the Sun, Earth, and Moon line up, combining their gravitational pull.

bank.prompt: What happens during a solar eclipse?
choices: The Moon blocks sunlight from Earth
Earth blocks light to the Moon
bank.answer: The Moon blocks sunlight from Earth
bank.explanation: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes directly between the Sun and Earth.

bank.prompt: What causes the different phases of the Moon?
choices: Viewing the lit Moon from angles
Earth’s shadow covering the Moon daily
The Moon spinning on a tilt
bank.answer: Viewing the lit Moon from angles
bank.explanation: Moon phases change as the Moon orbits Earth and we see different portions of its sunlit side.

bank.prompt: What causes a lunar eclipse?
choices: Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon
The Moon moves in front of Venus
bank.answer: Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon
bank.explanation: A lunar eclipse happens when Earth is directly between the Sun and a full Moon.

bank.prompt: When do moderate neap tides occur?
choices: During first and third quarter moons
When Earth is closest to Mars
bank.answer: During first and third quarter moons
bank.explanation: Neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon pull at right angles, making smaller tidal ranges.

bank.prompt: Why does Earth experience four seasons each year?
choices: Earth’s tilted axis as it orbits
Earth moving closer to the Moon
bank.answer: Earth’s tilted axis as it orbits
bank.explanation: Seasons happen because Earth’s axis is tilted 23.5 degrees as it revolves around the Sun.

bank.prompt: About how long does one full cycle of Moon phases take?
bank.explanation: A lunar cycle from one new moon to the next takes about 29.5 days.

principles.title: Matter & Energy Flow in Ecosystems & Biomes
principles.summary: Producers capture solar energy while matter cycles among organisms and the environment.

bank.prompt: What process do plants use to make food from sunlight?
bank.explanation: Photosynthesis uses sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make glucose sugar and oxygen.

bank.prompt: What is the role of decomposers in an ecosystem?
choices: Break down dead matter for nutrients
bank.answer: Break down dead matter for nutrients
bank.explanation: Decomposers like fungi and bacteria recycle nutrients from dead organisms back into the soil.

bank.prompt: What gas do plants release during photosynthesis?
bank.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen gas as a product of photosynthesis.

bank.prompt: How do cells release energy from sugar during respiration?
bank.explanation: Cellular respiration uses oxygen to break down glucose, releasing energy, water, and carbon dioxide.

bank.prompt: What happens to available energy moving up an energy pyramid?
choices: Most energy is lost as heat
bank.answer: Most energy is lost as heat
bank.explanation: Only about 10 percent of energy passes to the next level; the rest escapes as heat.

bank.prompt: Which two factors mainly define a land biome?
bank.explanation: A biome is a large region characterized by its average temperature, rainfall, and plant life.

bank.prompt: Which biome has permanently frozen soil called permafrost?
bank.explanation: The tundra is a cold, treeless biome with a frozen soil layer called permafrost.

bank.prompt: What are organisms that make their own food called?
bank.explanation: Producers make their own food using energy from sunlight and form the base of food webs.
